title: Space Data Link Security Protocol
organisation: Consultative Committee for Space Data Systems (CCSDS)
status_notes: Current issue according to the Document Control table (PDF p. 7): 355.0-B-2 (July 2022) adds USLP support and a normative reference to the SDLS Extended Procedures; the original issue 355.0-B-1 (September 2015) is marked superseded. Substantive changes are marked with change bars.
summary:
The CCSDS Recommended Standard for the **Space Data Link Security (SDLS) Protocol**, an optional security sublayer inside the Data Link Layer that adds authentication, encryption or authenticated encryption to the frames of the [TM](../ccsds/tm-sdlp.md), [TC](../ccsds/tc-sdlp.md), [AOS](../ccsds/aos.md) and (new in issue 2) [USLP](../ccsds/uslp.md) Space Data Link Protocols. It does not apply to Proximity-1, and it does not mandate any cryptographic algorithm: CCSDS 352.0 lists the recommended ones.

Section 2 explains the concept. A Security Association (SA) is a one-way, stateful cryptographic session bound to one or more Global Virtual Channels (GVCIDs) or, for TC and USLP, GMAP_IDs. Authentication uses a MAC over a masked part of the frame, with anti-replay sequence numbers checked against a window. Section 3 defines two abstract functions. ApplySecurity runs at the sending end. ProcessSecurity runs at the receiving end and returns a verification status code: invalid SPI, MAC failure, anti-replay failure or padding error. The section also lists the parameters of the SA database. Section 4 specifies the PDUs. The Security Header carries a 16-bit Security Parameter Index (SPI), followed by an optional Initialization Vector, Sequence Number and Pad Length, up to 64 octets in all. The Security Trailer carries the MAC. Section 4 also gives the SA management, sending and receiving procedures. Section 5 shows where the header and trailer sit in each frame type, and Table 5-1 says which data link services are protected. Section 6 (Table 6-1) lists the managed parameters, for example SPI 1-65534, IV 1-32 octets and MAC 8-64 octets. Annex A is the PICS proforma, Annex B covers security considerations (no key management, COP directives and the CLCW are unprotected) and Annex E gives baseline modes: AES-GCM for TM, AOS and USLP, and AES-CMAC for TC.

contents.title: Use of the Services with CCSDS Protocols

key_points.text: Issue 2 (July 2022) adds USLP support and a normative reference to the SDLS Extended Procedures (CCSDS 355.1-B-1); issue 1 (September 2015) is superseded.
The Security Protocol works only at the Data Link Layer (OSI layer 2), with the TM, TC, AOS and USLP Space Data Link Protocols. It is not applicable to Proximity-1.
The standard mandates no cryptographic algorithm; CCSDS 352.0-B-2 lists the recommended algorithms, and Annex E gives non-normative baseline implementations.

The Security Header is a mandatory 16-bit Security Parameter Index (SPI), followed by an optional Initialization Vector, Sequence Number and Pad Length (each fixed-length for the life of the SA). The whole header is at most 64 octets.
SPI values 0 (all zeros) and 65535 (all ones) are reserved by CCSDS; the managed-parameter range is 1-65534.
The Security Trailer, when present, holds only a fixed-length MAC; it is present whenever authentication or authenticated encryption is applied.

Every SA specifies exactly one service type: authentication, encryption, or authenticated encryption. A 'clear mode' SA with a no-op algorithm is possible for testing but not recommended in operations.
At the sending end, only one SA at a time can be active on a given GVCID or GMAP_ID. SAs are not created for Virtual Channels that carry Only Idle Data frames.
ProcessSecurity must at least distinguish these failure codes: no failure, invalid SPI, MAC verification failure, anti-replay sequence number failure, and padding error.
In a TM frame only the Frame Data is encrypted. The MAC covers the Primary Header, Secondary Header, Security Header and Frame Data, but not the ASM, OCF or ECF.
For TC, each SA must be associated with exactly one VC. The COP Management, VCF and MCF services are not protected.
Table 5-1 shows that the TM VC_FSH can be authenticated but not encrypted, and that the OCF-based services (VC_OCF, MC_OCF) are never protected.

Managed transmitted lengths: IV 1-32 octets, Sequence Number 2-8 octets, Pad Length 1-2 octets, MAC 8-64 octets. Authentication algorithms are HMAC, CMAC, GMAC, GCM or agency-specific; encryption algorithms are AES/Counter Mode, GCM or agency-specific.
The protocol gives no protection against jamming, traffic-flow analysis or false COP directives/CLCW contents, and it provides no key management.
The TM baseline is AES-GCM authenticated encryption with a 256-bit key, a 96-bit IV sent in-line and a 128-bit MAC, giving a 14-octet Security Header and a 16-octet Security Trailer.
The TC baseline is AES-CMAC authentication with a 256-bit key, a 32-bit anti-replay sequence number and a 128-bit MAC, giving a 6-octet Security Header and a 16-octet Security Trailer.
